entries.title: Soundness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)—→eval(𝛗)))
entries.comment: Soundness of the non-recursively-enumerable (non-r.e.) Henkin completion 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Why this avoids Tarski and Löb inconsistency: While the r.e. base theory 𝘛 cannot assert its own soundness without violating Gödel's second incompleteness theorem and Löb's theorem (hence soundness of 𝘛 is not postulated in 𝘛), the full theory 𝘍 is non-r.e. and Henkin-complete (Th(M)). The evaluation operator ⟦φ⟧ lives in the +1 metalogic on the base formula sublanguage Fm₀ without self-referential truth predicate internalisation, avoiding Tarski undefinability.

entries.comment: Semantic completeness of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍: for every sentence φ, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Together with Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72), this establishes (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ⇔ ⟦φ⟧, identifying 𝘍 as the complete true theory Th(M).

In classical logic, this is equivalent to (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ∨ (𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ). In the bivalent semantics of the background model M (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧), negation-completeness follows directly from semantic completeness and soundness.

entries.name: AxmSoundnessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Soundness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)—→eval(𝛗)))
entries.comment: Soundness of the non-recursively-enumerable (non-r.e.) Henkin completion 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Why this avoids Tarski and Löb inconsistency: While the r.e. base theory 𝘛 cannot assert its own soundness without violating Gödel's second incompleteness theorem and Löb's theorem (hence soundness of 𝘛 is not postulated in 𝘛), the full theory 𝘍 is non-r.e. and Henkin-complete (Th(M)). The evaluation operator ⟦φ⟧ lives in the +1 metalogic on the base formula sublanguage Fm₀ without self-referential truth predicate internalisation, avoiding Tarski undefinability.

entries.name: AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Semantic Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(eval(𝛗)—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Semantic completeness of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍: for every sentence φ, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Together with Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72), this establishes (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ⇔ ⟦φ⟧, identifying 𝘍 as the complete true theory Th(M).

entries.name: AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Negation-Completeness of the theory 𝘍

In classical logic, this is equivalent to (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ∨ (𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ). In the bivalent semantics of the background model M (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧), negation-completeness follows directly from semantic completeness and soundness.

entries.title: CoNecessitation(meta,WIP)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢‹𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗›)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: If a formula  is derived in 𝘍 from the empty context, then the formula 𝛗 is derived in 𝘍 from the context Γ. Why this holds for 𝘍: for an arbitrary theory 𝘞, concluding (𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗) from (𝘞, [] ⊢ ) requires 1-consistency / Σ₁-soundness of 𝘞 (and for the r.e. base theory 𝘛, asserting internal co-necessitation would by Löb's theorem 5.01 trivialize 𝘛). Because 𝘍 is a non-r.e. sound Henkin extension equipped with Soundness 3.73 ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) → ⟦ψ⟧), instantiating 3.73 at ψ :=  directly yields (𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗).

entries.title: Class comprehension axiom schema(meta,WIP)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)∀(x:Name)∀(k:Class.Expression)(Fm.FFI((k:Class.Expression),‹x›,𝛗)—→(𝘛,[]⊢‹(⟦k⟧∈{⦃x⦄|⟦𝛗⟧})←→((⟦k⟧ set)∧(let x = ⟦k⟧ in ⟦𝛗⟧))›)))

entries.name: ThmLoeb
entries.title: Löb's theorem(WIP)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(𝘌,[]⊢‹(𝘛,[]⊢‹(𝘛,[]⊢𝛗)—→⟦𝛗⟧›)—→(𝘛,[]⊢𝛗)›))
entries.comment: Here 𝘌 ∈ {IΣ₁, PA, 𝘛, NBG, MK} is an unspecified elementary metatheory capable of proving the Hilbert-Bernays-Löb derivability conditions D1-D3 for the r.e. base theory 𝘛 (specifically D3, Σ₁-completeness, which requires Σ₁-induction and fails in Robinson's arithmetic Q; see Hájek & Pudlák 1993, Metamathematics of First-Order Arithmetic, Ch. I §3 & Ch. III; Bezboruah & Shepherdson 1976, JSL 41(2):503-512; Boolos 1993, The Logic of Provability, Ch. 2).

entries.name: ThmSecondIncompleteness
entries.title: Gödel's second incompleteness theorem(WIP)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (𝘌,[]⊢‹(¬(𝘛,[]⊢‹⊥›))—→¬(𝘛,[]⊢‹¬(𝘛,[]⊢‹⊥›)›)›)
entries.comment: Formalized in the unspecified elementary metatheory 𝘌 ∈ {IΣ₁, PA, 𝘛, NBG, MK} (not Robinson's Q, which lacks Σ₁-induction needed for HBL condition D3; cf. Hájek & Pudlák 1993; Bezboruah & Shepherdson 1976) for the recursively enumerable object theory 𝘛. Note that Gödel's second incompleteness theorem applies to the r.e. theory 𝘛, whereas 𝘍 is non-r.e.
